title: Algorithmic Shortlisting in Participatory Budgeting
abstract: arXiv:2508.06577v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Participatory budgeting is a democratic innovation that allows citizens to propose and vote on public investment projects. To help organizers manage large volumes of submissions, we design and test privacy-preserving methods for algorithmic shortlisting. These algorithms predict which projects are likely to be funded using only project features and anonymous historical voting data. We demonstrate the limitations of a naive approach that uses a large language model to rank projects based on past success and propose a vote-based pipeline that enables state-of-the-art LLMs to perform on par with classical machine learning. Our findings indicate that user preferences in participatory budgeting are stable enough to allow algorithmic shortlisting to approximate an initial selection of projects effectively.

translated_title: 参与式预算中的算法初选
translated_abstract: 参与式预算是一项民主创新，允许公民对公共投资项目进行提议和投票。为了帮助组织者管理大量的项目提交，我们设计并测试了用于算法初选的隐私保护方法。这些算法仅利用项目特征和匿名的历史投票数据来预测哪些项目可能获得资助。我们展示了一种朴素方法的局限性，即直接使用大语言模型根据过往成功经验对项目进行排名，并提出了一种基于投票的流水线，使最先进的大语言模型能够达到与经典机器学习相当的性能。我们的研究结果表明，参与式预算中的用户偏好足够稳定，使得算法初选能够有效地近似项目的初步筛选。
tldr: 本文提出了基于匿名历史投票数据的隐私保护算法初选方法，通过基于投票的流水线使大语言模型达到与经典机器学习相当的性能，从而有效近似参与式预算项目的初步筛选。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes privacy-preserving algorithmic shortlisting methods based on anonymous historical voting data, and introduces a vote-based pipeline that enables state-of-the-art LLMs to perform on par with classical machine learning, effectively approximating initial project selection in participatory budgeting.
